title: pi-ui server REST surface
description: DTOs of the REST /api/v1 surface (docs/api-v1.md). Self-contained on purpose: server/scripts/gen.sh generates one Go file per schemas/*.json, so a cross-file $ref would produce code that does not compile; the shapes shared with core.json (device id, scope, timestamp) are therefore re-declared here with an Srv prefix. Objects are lenient: additionalProperties defaults to true and is never written out, so unknown fields survive a round trip and a newer client or server never breaks the other. This file pins the auth slice first; every later endpoint adds its own $defs here, in the same commit as its handler.

SrvProtocolVersion.description: REST protocol version, echoed in the X-Piui-Protocol header. A future v2 ships alongside v1 (dual support) instead of changing v1 shapes.

SrvDeviceId.description: Opaque device identifier minted by the server at pairing time and stored with the device record. Clients treat it as opaque and never parse it; it is what DELETE /auth/devices/{id} revokes and what auth.refresh keeps stable while the token rotates.

SrvScope.description: Authorization scope of one device token: viewer reads, operator drives sessions (prompt, bash, PTY, git write, file write), admin manages the server itself (devices, settings, MCP, updates, drain, audit). Every request is authorized against the scope stored with the device, never against a client-supplied value.

SrvTimestamp.description: RFC3339 timestamp. Expressed as a pattern instead of "format": "date-time" so codegen keeps it a string; a time.Time alias would not round-trip as text on the wire.

fingerprintSha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the leaf certificate, the value the app compares for TOFU pin confirmation (screens 4 of the mockup). A fingerprint that changes after pinning is a hard error, not a prompt.

notAfter.description: Certificate expiry, so the app can warn before a pinned certificate lapses.

SrvTlsInfo.description: TLS facts of the server. Present when the server terminates TLS itself or a proxy reports them; absent in plain-HTTP loopback mode.

piVersion.description: pi version the server was built and probed against. A mismatch degrades with a clear message instead of failing mid-run.

features.description: Capability flags the server advertises ("terminal", "git", "mcp", ...). Clients degrade gracefully when a flag is missing and ignore flags they do not know.

limits.description: Server limits as scalars (maxSessions, maxDevices, pairingTtlSec, replayEvents, ...). Open map so a new limit lands without a breaking schema change.

SrvServerIdentity.description: What a client learns about this server at pairing time and from GET /api/v1/server, so it can negotiate features, limits and certificate trust without a second round trip.

deviceName.description: Human-readable device name shown in the device list ("Alessandro's Pixel 9"). Chosen by the client, bounded by the server's maxDeviceNameLength.

platform.description: Free-form platform hint for diagnostics ("android", "linux", "windows"). The server never branches on it, so a new client platform needs no schema change.

code.description: One-time pairing code from the QR invite or typed by the user (screens 2-3 of the mockup). Single use, expires with the invite, rate-limited and audited; a consumed, unknown or expired code is a plain unauthorized failure with no hint of which.

secret.description: High-entropy secret carried only by the QR payload, never typed. It proves the client saw the actual invite screen rather than guessing a short code, which is what lets a typed 6-digit fallback stay rate-limited without being impossible to use.

password.description: Admin password, the second way in: it mints an admin-scoped device and is what recovers an installation with no enabled devices. Hash comparison is constant-time against the argon2id hash set with `pi-ui auth set-password`.

SrvPairRequest.description: POST /api/v1/auth/pair body. Exactly one credential: the pairing code (with the QR secret when it came from a scan) or the admin password. The response carries the device token exactly once; the server stores only its argon2id hash and the device record.

token.description: The device token, delivered exactly once and stored by the client in the OS keystore. Every later request sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the server keeps only its argon2id hash, so a database leak does not hand out working credentials.

expiresAt.description: Sliding expiry of the token. POST /auth/refresh rotates the token and extends it without changing the device id.

SrvPairResponse.description: POST /api/v1/auth/pair response. A pairing that yields operator scope never returns admin: admin requires the password branch.

token.description: The new device token. The previous one stops working the moment this response is written, which is what makes a refresh also a rotation: a leaked token has a bounded life.

SrvRefreshResponse.description: POST /api/v1/auth/refresh response. The device id and scope do not change; a revoked device is refused instead of refreshed.

name.description: Device name chosen at pairing time.

platform.description: Platform hint recorded at pairing time, when the client sent one.

lastSeenAt.description: Last authenticated request from this device, maintained by the auth middleware at a coarse granularity so the list can show inactive devices.

expiresAt.description: Current sliding expiry; a device past it is refused and shown as expired.

current.description: True for the device making the request, so the app can mark itself in the list without comparing ids it cannot see.

SrvDevice.description: One paired device as GET /api/v1/auth/devices reports it. Never carries the token or its hash; revocation is the only mutating operation and it takes effect immediately, closing the device's WebSockets too.

SrvDevicesResponse.description: GET /api/v1/auth/devices response, admin scope. Sorted by creation time so the first paired device reads first.
